synopsis: MIL tests a model of control logic against modeled machinery and surroundings, without real software or hardware, so rules can be checked before controller code is written [f13324, f13325]. It is the cheapest and earliest testing rung and can catch logical errors, such as warnings failing during articulation, while fixes still take minutes [f13326, f13330]. The recommended pipeline uses MIL and SIL for high-volume validation, targeting thousands of runs per night on cloud or on-premise compute [f7138, f13314, f13327]. Much of the relatively simple warn-then-brake logic can be designed and checked in late 2026 before sensor selection, but MIL provides no knowledge about sensors or real timing [f13332, f13329]. Tool options include a middle-cost chain reusing models across MIL, SIL and HIL, while IPG Automotive is reported to support off-highway testing through vehicle-in-the-loop with real tractors [f13328, f8652, f8807].
